description: The Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency publishes the main report of its 2022 Population and Housing Census, the first digital census and fifth since 1980, as a PDF of 259 pages. Chapter 9 on housing and living conditions, with appendix tables, covers tenure, dwelling type, and wall, roof and floor materials such as burnt bricks, pole and dagga and cement blocks. The electricity table counts 3,818,734 households: 1,228,359 on the national grid, 58,449 on local mini-grids, 1,057,075 on solar power and 1,453,618 with no electricity. Other tables cover lighting and cooking energy, drinking and general-use water with the time taken to reach the source, toilets from flush to sewer or septic tank to pit latrines and open defecation, handwashing, solid waste disposal and home internet. Housing tables are by province and by rural or urban area. Coverage is national. Format and access: free PDF, no registration; a separate PDF gives population and households by district and ward. Licence: none found. Caveats: housing tables stop at province level; the NADA archive reset the connection from the cloud, so census microdata could not be checked; the round 1 visit read only the homepage. Simulation uses: grid, mini-grid and solar shares for electrification and resilience planning, and sewer and septic shares for wastewater capacity. Related records: none closer in the catalogue.

schema_summary: Chapter 9 (pages 74 to 99) and Appendix VIII tables: 9.1 tenure; dwelling type; 9.3 wall material (burnt bricks, pole and dagga, cement blocks, unburnt bricks); roof and floor material; rooms and sleeping rooms; 9.7 households by electricity source (national grid, local mini-grid, solar power, generator, wind, biogas, none); 9.8 lighting energy; 9.9 cooking energy; 9.10 drinking water source by time to source; 9.11 general-use water; 9.12 toilet type (flush to sewer, septic tank, VIP, pit latrines, none); 9.14 handwashing; solid waste disposal; ICT gadgets and home internet. By province and rural or urban area.
